**Juan Pablo Henao** is an applied environmental economist working on water economics and
water governance. He is a doctoral candidate and research associate at the Chair of Agricultural
Production and Resource Economics, Technical University of Munich.

His research covers water pricing and cost recovery under the EU Water Framework Directive,
environmentally sustainable productivity growth in EU agriculture, and the efficiency of
irrigation water management. He combines optimisation, stochastic frontier analysis, data
envelopment analysis and econometrics in R. In the Horizon Europe project RETOUCH NEXUS he leads
the work on water governance indicators, building on the OECD Principles on Water Governance.

Before TUM he worked for three years at FAO in Rome, designing environment and climate projects
for Global Environment Facility funding in Latin America and the Caribbean and in Eastern Europe
and Central Asia. Earlier, at CEDE, Universidad de los Andes, he valued ecosystem services and
coastal nature-based solutions and studied artisanal fisheries in marine protected areas. He holds
an M.Sc. in Applied Economics and a B.Sc. in Mathematics from Universidad de los Andes.
